name: Mel Gibson
milestone_by_age_26: Starred in Mad Max (1979), which became the highest-grossing Australian film to date, and won the Australian Film Institute Best Actor Award for Tim (1979).
early_history_summary: Gibson moved from New York to Sydney at age 12 and entered NIDA with no prior acting experience after his sister submitted an application on his behalf. He made his film debut in Summer City (1977) while still a student, graduated NIDA that year, and immediately landed the lead in Mad Max (1979), which grossed over $100 million worldwide and launched his international career.
family_context_summary: Born sixth of 11 children in Peekskill, NY to Hutton Gibson, a writer and Jeopardy champion, and Irish-born Anne Reilly. Paternal grandfather was a millionaire tobacco businessman. Family moved to Australia in 1968 to avoid Vietnam War draft.
parent_family_domain_summary: Father Hutton Gibson was a writer and Catholic traditionalist, not connected to film or entertainment. No documented family domain advantage in acting.
primary_early_advantage_tags: Australian New Wave,NIDA training,large family,structural wave
evidence_summary: Gibson leveraged NIDA training and the Australian New Wave cinema movement to achieve breakout success by age 23. His family had some means (grandfather was a millionaire, father a Jeopardy champion) but no entertainment industry connections. The structural wave of Australian cinema in the late 1970s was a key catalyst, and his natural screen presence impressed directors immediately despite no prior acting experience.
starting_point: Born to a large Irish-American Catholic family in Peekskill, NY; father was a writer and WWII veteran, grandfather a millionaire tobacco businessman; family relocated to Australia when he was 12.
current_position: Active actor-director with net worth ~$425 million; appointed Special Ambassador to Hollywood by President Trump in January 2025; recently directed Flight Risk (2025).

trajectory.event: Made film debut in Summer City while still a student at NIDA in Sydney.
Starred in Mad Max, which became the highest-grossing Australian film to date, and won the AFI Best Actor Award for Tim.
Starred in Peter Weir's Gallipoli, winning a second AFI Best Actor Award.
Launched the Lethal Weapon franchise, cementing his status as a global action star.
Won the Academy Award for Best Director for Braveheart, which also won Best Picture.
Directed and produced The Passion of the Christ, which grossed over $600 million worldwide.
Appointed Special Ambassador to Hollywood by President Trump; directed Flight Risk starring Mark Wahlberg.

name: Katrine Lunde
milestone_by_age_26: Won the 2004 European Women's Handball Championship gold medal with Norway, her first major international title.
early_history_summary: Lunde started playing handball at age 9-10 with her twin sister Kristine in Kristiansand, Norway, where the local team played in the third league. She debuted for the Norwegian national team in September 2002 at age 22 and won her first European Championship gold in 2004 at age 24, establishing herself as Norway's first-choice goalkeeper.
family_context_summary: Born in Kristiansand, Norway to a non-sporting family; father reportedly almost hated sports. Grew up with twin sister Kristine Lunde, who also became a Norwegian international handball player. Father supported them by buying handball goals for summer training.
parent_family_domain_summary: No family background in sports; father was not a sports enthusiast but supported the twins' handball training with equipment. No documented parental domain expertise in athletics.
primary_early_advantage_tags: twin sister partnership,Norwegian handball system,early specialization,non-sporting family
evidence_summary: Lunde's primary early advantage was her twin sister Kristine, who trained and played alongside her from age 9 through their professional careers. They came from a non-sporting family in a small Norwegian city with limited elite sport infrastructure. Norway's dominant women's handball program provided the elite pipeline, and Lunde's sustained practice from childhood gave her the reps needed to reach the national team by 22 and win European gold by 24.
starting_point: Born in Kristiansand, Norway to a non-sporting family; father almost hated sports but supported the twins' handball training with goals at their summer cabin.
current_position: Retired from professional handball in April 2026 after final national team appearance; widely regarded as the greatest handball goalkeeper of all time with 3 Olympic golds, 3 World Championship titles, and 7 European Championship golds.

trajectory.event: Debuted for the Norwegian national team against Yugoslavia on September 26.
Won her first European Championship gold medal with Norway.
Won Olympic gold at the Beijing Olympics and was named to the tournament All-Star Team.
Won her first EHF Champions League title with Viborg HK.
Won her first World Championship gold medal with Norway.
Won her third Olympic gold at the Paris Olympics and was named tournament MVP.
Won the World Championship in her final international tournament, named best goalkeeper of the tournament.

name: Kurt Diemberger
milestone_by_age_26: Made the first ascent of Broad Peak (8,051m) in 1957 in lightweight style without oxygen or porters, a landmark achievement in Himalayan mountaineering.
early_history_summary: Diemberger grew up in Villach, Austria, and fell in love with mountaineering at age 16. He spent his summers climbing in the Alps, and between 1956 and 1958 climbed the three hardest north faces of the Alps (Matterhorn, Eiger, Grandes Jorasses) with partner Wolfgang Stefan. In 1957, at age 25, he joined Hermann Buhl's four-person expedition for the first ascent of Broad Peak, becoming one of the few mountaineers to make a first ascent of an 8,000m peak.
family_context_summary: Born in Villach, Austria; son of a teacher. Grew up in the Alps with direct access to mountaineering. Attended university in Vienna, obtaining an MBA in 1955 and M.Ed in 1962. Chose his field of study partly for the long vacations that allowed mountaineering.
parent_family_domain_summary: Father was a teacher; no documented family background in mountaineering. However, growing up in Villach in the Austrian Alps provided natural proximity to climbing.
primary_early_advantage_tags: Austrian Alps,alpine climbing,Hermann Buhl partnership,lightweight style
evidence_summary: Diemberger's primary advantage was growing up in Villach, Austria, surrounded by the Alps, which gave him direct mountain immersion from age 16. His partnership with legendary mountaineer Hermann Buhl was the critical network advantage that brought him onto the Broad Peak expedition. He had limited financial resources as a student, borrowing his grandfather's bicycle to cycle to the Matterhorn, but his deep alpine experience (three north faces of the Alps by 1958) made him one of the most skilled young mountaineers of his generation.
starting_point: Born in Villach, Austria, son of a teacher; grew up in the Alps and discovered mountaineering at age 16, cycling to climbs on his grandfather's borrowed bicycle.
current_position: Living at age 94 in Italy; still active in mountaineering film projects with his daughter; the only living person to have made first ascents of two 8,000m peaks.

trajectory.event: Made the first ascent of Broad Peak (8,051m) in lightweight style without oxygen or porters.
Made the first ascent of Dhaulagiri (8,167m) with a Swiss team, becoming one of only three people to make first ascents of two 8,000m peaks.
Climbed both Makalu and Everest in the same year.
Climbed K2 but was trapped in a storm on descent; companion Julie Tullis died and Diemberger suffered severe frostbite requiring amputations.
Received the Piolet d'Or Lifetime Achievement Award, mountaineering's highest honor.

name: Nikolay Shmatko
milestone_by_age_26: Became a sculptor at age 33; no material artistic milestone by age 26 found. Previously worked as a firefighter and poster artist.
early_history_summary: Shmatko was born in the Donetsk region of Ukraine and worked as a firefighter and poster artist before becoming a sculptor at age 33. He had no formal art training and began sculpting when asked to create a marble bas-relief for a gravestone, discovering an innate ability for working with marble.
family_context_summary: Born in the Donetsk region of Ukraine. Not documented in reviewed sources.
evidence_summary: Shmatko did not begin sculpting until age 33, having previously worked as a firefighter and poster artist. No material artistic milestone by age 26 is documented. His artistic career began with a gravestone commission and developed through self-taught marble working.

name: Gerrie Knetemann
milestone_by_age_26: Won the Amstel Gold Race in 1974, his debut professional season, a major one-day cycling classic.
early_history_summary: Knetemann grew up in Amsterdam and worked as a road builder while racing as an amateur cyclist. He accumulated amateur wins from 1968 to 1973 (including 11 wins in 1973 alone), then turned professional in 1974 with the French Gan-Mercier team. In his very first professional season, he won the Amstel Gold Race, a prestigious Dutch cycling classic, at age 23.
family_context_summary: Born in Amsterdam, Netherlands; worked as a road builder (stratenmaker) in his youth. Little formal education. Married Gre Donker, also a racing cyclist. Working-class background.
parent_family_domain_summary: Not documented in reviewed sources. No evidence of family cycling background.
primary_early_advantage_tags: amateur racing,road builder,Dutch cycling culture,Gan-Mercier team
evidence_summary: Knetemann came from a working-class Amsterdam background with no documented family cycling connections. He built his career through years of amateur racing while working as a road builder, accumulating 29 amateur wins from 1968 to 1973. The Dutch cycling ecosystem and his signing with the professional Gan-Mercier team (alongside Zoetemelk and Poulidor) provided the platform for his immediate impact in his 1974 debut season, winning the Amstel Gold Race at age 23.
starting_point: Born in Amsterdam, Netherlands to a working-class family; worked as a road builder before turning professional cyclist.
current_position: Died on November 2, 2004 at age 53 from a heart attack while mountain biking near Bergen, Netherlands; was serving as national coach of the Dutch cycling federation (KNWU).

trajectory.event: Won the Amstel Gold Race in his debut professional season with Gan-Mercier team.
Won his first Tour de France stage.
Won the UCI Road World Championship and Paris-Nice; wore the yellow jersey in the Tour de France.
Won the Amstel Gold Race for a second time after recovering from a serious cycling accident.
Died of a heart attack while mountain biking; was serving as Dutch national cycling coach.

name: Ferenc Krausz
milestone_by_age_26: No material milestone by age 26 found. Krausz was still a PhD student at Budapest University of Technology and TU Wien during his mid-twenties; his major breakthroughs (attosecond pulse generation) came in 2001 and his Nobel Prize in 2023.
early_history_summary: Krausz studied electrical engineering and physics in Budapest before beginning PhD studies in laser physics in 1985 at age 23. He moved to TU Wien for his PhD, which he completed with distinction in 1991 at age 29. His pioneering attosecond physics work came in the early 2000s, leading to the 2023 Nobel Prize in Physics.
family_context_summary: Born in Mor, Hungary. Studied at Budapest University of Technology and Eotvos Lorand University. Not documented in reviewed sources regarding family financial status.
evidence_summary: Krausz was still in early PhD studies by age 26, with no material research milestone. His career-defining work in attosecond physics came in the 2000s, and his Nobel Prize in Physics was awarded in 2023 at age 61. No independently verifiable milestone by age 26 was found.

name: Vladimir Posner
milestone_by_age_26: No material milestone by age 26 found. Posner worked as a freelance translator and literary secretary before starting his journalism career at Novosti Press Agency in 1961 at age 27. His fame came with Cold War-era television spacebridges in the 1980s.
early_history_summary: Posner was born in France, fled to the US in 1940, and moved to Moscow in 1949. He worked as a freelance translator (1959-60) and literary secretary to poet Samuel Marshak (1960-61) before beginning his journalism career at Novosti Press Agency in 1961 at age 27. He became famous in the 1980s through US-Soviet television spacebridges.
family_context_summary: Born in France to a Russian-born father who worked for Soviet intelligence and a French mother. Moved to the US in 1940, then to East Germany and Moscow. Multilingual upbringing (English, French, Russian).
parent_family_domain_summary: Father Vladimir Pozner Sr. worked in the cinema section of the US War Department and was recruited by Soviet intelligence. Family had connections to Soviet cultural and intelligence circles, but no direct journalism background.
evidence_summary: Posner did not begin his journalism career until age 27 in 1961. Before that, he worked as a freelance translator and literary secretary. His fame came decades later through Cold War television broadcasts. No material milestone by age 26 was found.

name: Betty Williams
milestone_by_age_26: No material milestone by age 26 found. Williams was an office receptionist before co-founding the Community of Peace People in August 1976 at age 33, which led to the 1976 Nobel Peace Prize.
early_history_summary: Williams was born in Belfast to a Protestant father and Catholic mother. She worked as an office receptionist after completing her education at St Dominic's Grammar School. She joined an anti-violence campaign in the early 1970s, but her defining moment came in August 1976 when she witnessed the deaths of three children and co-founded the Community of Peace People, leading to the Nobel Peace Prize at age 33.
family_context_summary: Born in Belfast, Northern Ireland. Father was a butcher, mother was a housewife. Protestant father and Catholic mother, which she credited for her religious tolerance. Married at age 18 in 1961.
parent_family_domain_summary: No family background in activism or public life. Father was a butcher, mother a housewife. Working-class background in Belfast.
evidence_summary: Williams was an office receptionist with no notable public achievements before age 26. Her peace activism began in the early 1970s when she was in her late twenties, and her Nobel Prize-winning work came in 1976 at age 33. No material milestone by age 26 was found.

name: Didier Drogba
milestone_by_age_26: Scored 17 goals in 34 Ligue 1 appearances for Guingamp in the 2002-03 season, establishing himself as a top striker in French football and earning a transfer to Olympique de Marseille.
early_history_summary: Drogba was born in Abidjan and sent to France at age 5 to live with his uncle Michel Goba, a professional footballer. He moved between Ivory Coast and France multiple times due to family economic hardship. He joined Le Mans as an apprentice at 19, signed his first professional contract at 21 in 1999, and after struggling with injuries, moved to Guingamp where he broke out with 17 goals in the 2002-03 Ligue 1 season at age 24-25, earning a transfer to Marseille.
family_context_summary: Born in Abidjan, Ivory Coast to parents who worked as low-income bankers. Sent to France at age 5 to live with uncle Michel Goba, a professional footballer. Parents lost their jobs, causing additional moves. Grew up in economic hardship, separated from parents for extended periods.
parent_family_domain_summary: Uncle Michel Goba was a professional footballer in France's Ligue 2 who served as Drogba's mentor and father figure. Goba converted Drogba from right-back to striker and guided his early football development. No documented parental football expertise.
primary_early_advantage_tags: uncle mentor,economic hardship,late developer,French football system,physical talent
evidence_summary: Drogba's early career was shaped by significant adversity: separation from parents at age 5, economic hardship, multiple country moves, and injuries that delayed his development. His uncle Michel Goba, a professional footballer, provided crucial mentorship and domain exposure. Drogba was a late developer who didn't sign professionally until 21, but his physical talent and determination drove a breakout 2002-03 season at Guingamp (17 Ligue 1 goals) that launched his path to Chelsea and global stardom.
starting_point: Born in Abidjan, Ivory Coast to low-income banker parents; sent to France at age 5 to live with uncle Michel Goba, a professional footballer, due to economic hardship.
current_position: Retired from professional football in 2018 at age 40; net worth ~$90 million; serves as Vice President of Peace and Sport and co-owner of Phoenix Rising FC.

trajectory.event: Scored 17 goals in 34 Ligue 1 appearances for Guingamp, earning a transfer to Olympique de Marseille.
Signed for Chelsea for £24 million after scoring 19 goals and reaching the UEFA Cup Final with Marseille.
Named African Footballer of the Year for the first time.
Scored the equalizer and winning penalty in the Champions League Final for Chelsea against Bayern Munich.
Retired from professional football after playing for Phoenix Rising as player-owner.
Serves as Vice President of Peace and Sport and runs the Didier Drogba Foundation.

name: Stefan Hell
milestone_by_age_26: No material milestone by age 26 found. Hell was a physics student at Heidelberg University, completing his diploma in 1987 at age 24-25. His PhD came in 1990 at age 28, and his breakthrough STED microscopy work in the 2000s led to the 2014 Nobel Prize in Chemistry.
early_history_summary: Hell grew up in Romania and moved to West Germany in 1978 at age 15. He studied physics at Heidelberg University from 1981, completing his diploma in 1987. His PhD on confocal microscopy was completed in 1990 at age 28. His groundbreaking STED microscopy concept was developed in the 1990s and experimentally proven in 2000, leading to the 2014 Nobel Prize in Chemistry.
family_context_summary: Born in Arad, Romania to ethnic German parents. Family moved to West Germany in 1978, settling in Ludwigshafen. Father's job was becoming uncertain and mother was diagnosed with serious illness, which influenced Hell's practical choice of research topic.
parent_family_domain_summary: Not documented in reviewed sources. No evidence of parental scientific or academic background.
evidence_summary: Hell was still a university student by age 26, having completed his diploma in physics in 1987. His PhD was completed in 1990 at age 28, and his Nobel Prize-winning STED microscopy work came in the 1990s-2000s. No material research milestone by age 26 was found.

name: Juan Manuel Márquez
milestone_by_age_26: No material world-title milestone by age 26 found. Márquez won the WBO NABO Featherweight regional title in 1997 at age 23-24, but his first world championship came in 2004 at age 31. His fame arrived with world titles and the Pacquiao fights after age 30.
early_history_summary: Márquez made his professional boxing debut at age 19 on May 29, 1993. He compiled a 29-1 record over six years and won the WBO NABO Featherweight title in 1997, which he defended seven times. He was called 'the best fighter without a world title' but did not win his first world championship until 2004 at age 31. He worked as an accountant while training during this period.
family_context_summary: Comes from a boxing family in Mexico City; brother Rafael Márquez was also a world champion boxer (bantamweight and super bantamweight). Trained under renowned trainer Ignacio Beristáin. Worked as an accountant while building his boxing career.
parent_family_domain_summary: Brother Rafael Márquez was a world champion boxer, indicating a family boxing culture. Trained under Ignacio Beristáin, one of Mexico's most respected boxing trainers.
evidence_summary: Márquez had a respectable professional record by age 26 (approximately 29-1 with a regional NABO title), but no world championship or material global milestone. His first world title came in 2004 at age 31, and his fame was built on world titles and the legendary Pacquiao trilogy in his thirties. The NABO title is a regional feeder title, not a world championship.

name: David James
milestone_by_age_26: Won the Football League Cup with Liverpool in 1995 as the club's first-choice goalkeeper, and was an FA Cup runner-up with Liverpool in 1996 at age 25.
early_history_summary: James grew up in Welwyn Garden City and signed for Watford schoolboys at age 13. He turned professional on his 18th birthday in 1988, made his senior debut for Watford in August 1990 at age 20, and was signed by Liverpool for £1 million in July 1992 at age 21. He became Liverpool's first-choice goalkeeper and won the League Cup in 1995 at age 24, establishing himself in the Premier League.
family_context_summary: Born in Welwyn Garden City, Hertfordshire; mixed Jamaican and English descent; seventh of eight children. Parents separated when he was around two. Grew up with mother and maternal grandparents. Experienced racial bullying as the only non-white child at his primary school.
parent_family_domain_summary: No documented family background in football. Grew up supporting Luton Town. Parents separated early; working-class background.
primary_early_advantage_tags: Watford academy,Liverpool signing,physical stature,working-class background,Premier League era
evidence_summary: James entered football through Watford's academy system at age 13, spending seven years as a schoolboy and apprentice before turning professional. His physical attributes (6'4" frame) and academy training earned him a £1m move to Liverpool at 21. He won the League Cup with Liverpool at 24 and reached the FA Cup final at 25. His background was working-class with early family separation and racial bullying, but the Watford-Liverpool pipeline provided the elite platform for his early career.
starting_point: Born in Welwyn Garden City to a mixed Jamaican-English working-class family; parents separated when he was two; seventh of eight children; experienced racial bullying in childhood.
current_position: Retired from professional football; net worth ~$15 million; works as a football pundit on Sky Sports; appointed MBE in 2012 for services to football and charity.

trajectory.event: Signed for Liverpool for £1 million and became the club's first-choice goalkeeper.
Won the Football League Cup with Liverpool.
Made his debut for the England national team.
Won the FA Cup with Portsmouth, his first FA Cup winner's medal.
Became the oldest goalkeeper to appear in an FA Cup Final; played at the FIFA World Cup for England.
Appointed MBE in the Queen's Birthday Honours for services to football and charity.
